learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to map a mechanical system to a model.
They can apply the basic static principles to the model and set up the model equations (force / moment equilibrium).
Students are able to solve the model equations, evaluate the results, and check their plausibility.

syllabus_topics: Mechanical modeling, abstraction, force, rigid body, cutting principle ("free-body diagram"), law of interaction, physical quantities and units
Forces with a common point of application, decomposition of forces in the plane, component representation, equilibrium in the plane, central force system in space
General force systems, equilibrium of a rigid body, force system in the plane and in space, moment of a force, resultant, parallel displacement of forces
Centers of gravity of bodies and areas
Bearing reactions, planar structures, static determinacy, multi-part structures
Truss, static determinacy, construction, determination of bar forces
Internal forces on straight beams and frames
Concept of work, determination of equilibrium positions, stability
Adhesion and friction, Coulomb's laws of friction, rope adhesion and rope friction
assessment_rules: The form of examination (written examination or project/topic presentation and short/understanding questions) will be announced at the beginning of the lecture. Credit points are awarded upon passing the module examination. The grade is weighted according to ECTS credit points.
bibliography: Gross/Hauger/Schnell: Technische Mechanik, Band 1 Statik, Springer Verlag
Gross et al.: Formeln und Aufgaben zur Technischen Mechanik 1, SPRINGER ebook
